note: Morton County campground on ND 1806 about 28 miles south of Mandan, beside the Fort Rice State Historic Site. The county's boat ramps and primitive camping area are at the Fort Rice Recreation Area on Boat Dock Road, near the Missouri River. --Claude
summary: Morton County pages read: $25 electric / $15 primitive (stored note said $20/$10), 10 electric sites (50/30/20 A, no water at sites), first come first served, 14 days in any 30, vault toilets/water/dump. Groups written; note cleaned. Riverview -> not waterfront (river ~700+ m away). Name/phone flags.
flags: WATERFRONT DOWNGRADE: riverview -> not waterfront (not an --AWH value). The electric loop at 46.5128,-100.5871 is set among fields and tree belts; the nearest water is a small slough ~450 m south, and the Missouri River (head of Lake Oahe) channel and its marsh are ~600-800 m south-east across pasture and floodplain. No pad has a view across open ground at the ~50-250 m scale. The county's boat ramps and primitive camping are at the separate Fort Rice Recreation Area on Boat Dock Rd, not at the electric loop.

NAME: the entry is named 'Fort Rice Recreation Area', but the pin and the 10 electric sites are the county's 'Fort Rice Campground' (830 Campground St.); the 'Recreation Area' (781 Boat Dock Rd.) is the boat-ramp site with vault toilets and primitive camping only. Suggest renaming to 'Fort Rice Campground'. Not proposed as a split: the boat-ramp area has no designated sites.
PIN: stored 46.51272,-100.58732 is on the campground loop: ok.
PHONE: none stored -> 701-667-3363 (Morton County Parks office, on the county pages).
WEBSITE: keep https://www.mortonnd.gov/fortrice (Google lists mortonnd.org/fortrice, which redirects to the same county site).

LONG-STAY: a 2020 county notice on the page designated the four pull-through sites for reservable 30-day stays ($350); the current Parks page says camping is limited to 14 days in any rolling 30 and individual sites cannot be reserved. The current rule was written; the 2020 notice looks superseded. County-run, not a private park.
COUNT: HHS lists 25 units (likely counting primitive spaces); the county names 10 electric sites. Wrote 10 with a note.
RATING: Google 3.3 from 4 reviews (public campground, too few for the review rule).
